subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Leadership, Coaching, and Inclusive Event Design
title: Reteach and varied practice: designing an event for genuinely mixed abilities under transfer
focus: designing an event for genuinely mixed abilities
essentialQuestion: How do I design an activity where the least confident person present has a good time?
materials: equipment appropriate to the designed session
privacySafeScenario: Design and facilitate one small inclusive activity session, then evaluate it against stated inclusion and safety criteria and revise the design.
studentTask: Learner works designing an event for genuinely mixed abilities while running the event for real, evaluated by whether the least confident person present had a good time at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of designing an event for genuinely mixed abilities degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner holds designing an event for genuinely mixed abilities while running the event for real, evaluated by whether the least confident person present had a good time, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
adaptationChoices: The session may be run for one person, for a household group, or delivered as a complete plan with a rehearsed walk-through if no participants are available.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of designing an event for genuinely mixed abilities yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
The session may be run for one person, for a household group, or delivered as a complete plan with a rehearsed walk-through if no participants are available.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where designing an event for genuinely mixed abilities shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
